questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How social media is changing in the age of AI
How to become famous on social media
The history of Morse code
Why young people prefer Facebook
questions.why: Pippa says they'll discuss how social media is changing in the age of AI.

questions.q: According to Pippa, what did people use early social media for?
options: Mainly for serious political debate
Finding jobs and new business contacts
Posting messages and photos for friends
Watching films and TV series online
questions.why: She says they were places to post messages to friends or share photos of your breakfast.

questions.q: Why do Tristan and Asma think the picture of a man and his dog was made by AI?
options: It had a small label saying it was made by AI
The man looked half like Jesus, half like his dog
The photo was in black and white
The dog in the picture was talking
questions.why: They say he looks like Jesus and like his dog, so he 'has to be AI-ed'.

questions.q: What did a recent report find about social media activity?
options: It has doubled since 2022 across all apps
It is higher than ever before among teens
It stopped almost completely in 2016
It peaked in 2022 and has fallen since
questions.why: Neil says a report found social media activity peaked in 2022 and has been going down ever since.

questions.q: When did Kyle Chayka feel that social media changed?
options: In 2015–2016, during the US election debate
When Facebook was first created at university
When the website MySpace finally closed
Only last year, with the rise of AI content
questions.why: He says in 2015/2016 Twitter became the hub of election discourse in the US.

questions.q: What does Kyle suggest about how the internet felt before that time?
options: It was boring and slow to use at home
It was far too dangerous for young people
It seemed a fun place to make friends
It was only used for work and study
questions.why: He says it shattered the illusion that the internet was a place to have fun and find cool friends.

questions.q: What does Kyle think about AI-generated content on social media?
options: It's exactly what users really want to see
It's new now, but people will lose interest
It will soon be banned by most governments
It will replace all human creators soon
questions.why: He says users don't really want it: 'it's a novelty for now and people will drift away'.

questions.q: What does Kyle predict people will do in future?
options: Post more than ever before
Stop using the internet completely
Use only the biggest platforms
Move to smaller online spaces and post less
questions.why: He sees people gravitating towards smaller spaces, individual voices, and 'posting less in general'.
